profile.reading: Per Cologix own site, this Jacksonville, Florida facility (JAX1) sits at 421 West Church Street and totals 11,000 square feet. The page states 5 kW plus per cabinet but does not give a total facility power capacity in MW. JAX1 is a relatively small edge facility within Cologix's national footprint, at 11,000 square feet against a portfolio that includes buildings as large as 455,000 square feet (Ashburn ASH1) elsewhere in this registry; the operator markets per-cabinet power density (5 kW-plus per cabinet) rather than a total facility MW figure for this size of facility, a pattern this registry has also observed at Cologix's other smaller edge sites. Cologix is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, operational since December 2010, and describes itself as North America's leading network-neutral interconnection and hyperscale edge data center company, with more than 45 facilities across 13 North American markets serving roughly 2,000 customers with access to more than 725 networks and more than 350 cloud service providers, per the operator's own materials; Jacksonville and nearby Lakeland, Florida are among the company's confirmed US markets. The company grew through a series of acquisitions beginning in 2010, including Navisite, The Minnesota Gateway, Canix, MetroOptic in 2019, vXchnge in 2020-2021, and Cyxtera in 2023, the last of which connects to the separate Cyxtera operator record tracked elsewhere in this registry. No year-opened date specific to JAX1 was located in sourcing reachable this session. Downtown Jacksonville has developed a modest colocation and interconnection presence in recent years, anchored by facilities like this one, distinct from the much larger data center clusters in Atlanta or Northern Virginia, reflecting Cologix's general strategy of placing smaller edge facilities in secondary metros to shorten last-mile latency for regional customers.

reading.body:
Cologix Jacksonville JAX1 is an 11,000 square foot facility in downtown Jacksonville marketed at 5 kW per cabinet, a density suggesting roughly 220 to 440 cabinets depending on whether the stated minimum applies uniformly. The operator publishes no total facility power capacity in megawatts for this site. This is characteristic of Cologix's approach to smaller edge facilities, where per-cabinet density replaces total MW disclosure.

JAX1 ranks fifth among Florida's facilities with any published capacity figure and holds an unknown share of the state's mapped 13 facilities because the operator has not stated its total power draw. Four facilities in Florida publish megawatt figures totaling 9.35 MW, a constraint that makes each additional megawatt visible to the market significant for tracking state-level growth. JAX1's silence on total capacity means its actual footprint in that total is not disclosed.

The facility qualifies for network-neutral colocation and hyperscale edge service within Cologix's national portfolio of 45 sites. It sits in a secondary metro strategy, distinct from the much larger clusters anchoring Atlanta or Northern Virginia. Without published power capacity, JAX1 cannot be ranked against other AI-relevant infrastructure by the metric that matters most to scaling: the megawatt.
